claim: With one static RLS rule on `orders` (column `tenant_id`, value `acme`), `apply_rls` returns exactly the expected output for each of exactly these five inputs — complete by construction: - PostgreSQL, `SELECT "quote_ident"(name) FROM orders` → `SELECT "quote_ident"(name) FROM orders WHERE orders.tenant_id = 'acme'` - PostgreSQL, `SELECT "MyFunc"(name) FROM orders` → `SELECT "MyFunc"(name) FROM orders WHERE orders.tenant_id = 'acme'` - PostgreSQL, `SELECT public."MyFunc"(name) FROM orders` → `SELECT public."MyFunc"(name) FROM orders WHERE orders.tenant_id = 'acme'` - MySQL, ``SELECT `MyFunc`(name) FROM orders`` → ``SELECT `MyFunc`(name) FROM orders WHERE orders.tenant_id = 'acme'`` - SQLite, `SELECT "MyFunc"(name) FROM orders` → `SELECT "MyFunc"(name) FROM orders WHERE orders.tenant_id = 'acme'`
